correctness.rationale: The derivative identity follows coefficient-by-coefficient from the entire Mittag-Leffler series. Integrating it gives unit mass for \(\lambda x^{\alpha-1}E_{\alpha,\alpha}(-\lambda x^\alpha)\), hence mass \(\alpha\) for the source expression. The source's own survival asymptotic and the nonnegative tail integral give the sharp moment condition \(r<\alpha\). The likelihood correction follows from the exact multiplicative relation \(f_{\rm pub}=\alpha f_*\).

value.rationale: Normalization is foundational: for typical plotted values such as \(\alpha=0.5\), the claimed PDF carries only half of total probability. The same defect propagates to the survival calculation and likelihood, while the heavy tail eliminates every positive integer moment in the genuinely fractional regime. Recognizing the normalized model as a classical Mittag-Leffler law also prevents a new-family interpretation of an already established distribution.
